correctness.rationale: For n≥2 a nonempty hub-free fort must select both endpoints and have no adjacent omissions; the hub then sees at least two selected vertices. These path conditions are upward-closed among subsets, so testing individual deletions here suffices: an interior 1 can be removed exactly when flanked by 1's. With the hub selected, the remaining selected path set must dominate the path. A minimal dominator can contain a path fort only by being that fort. In a path fort no omitted vertex is private to a selected vertex; minimal domination therefore requires every selected vertex to be isolated among selected vertices. This leaves precisely the odd endpoint-to-endpoint alternating word. For the dominator series, singleton runs self-witness, while each end of a doubleton run needs a private zero: an internal gap incident to such a run has length 2, and an external gap incident to it has length 1. All remaining gaps are those permitted by domination. The resulting two-state transfer matrix has determinant 1−z²−z³−z⁴+z⁶ and gives the stated series; the one-or-two 1-block construction gives F. The declared n=0,1 conventions also agree with the series. Independent adjacency/proper-subset enumeration over all 262121 nonempty fan subsets for 2≤n≤16 matched both exact families; independent private-neighborhood tests and series coefficients matched at those orders, giving minimal-fort totals 3,2,6,5,10,12,18,24,34,47,65,90,125,173,240. Replay: python3 /workspace/reproductions/check_fan_crown_skew.py fan. The supplied code's expansion to 100 is not comparison to independent counts past 16; neither bounded run proves the general theorem.

evidence: With the hub white, the absence of blue endpoint pairs and blue consecutive triples means precisely that every blue path vertex has a white path neighbor; thus the white path part dominates. Inclusion-minimize the dominating path parts and remove those containing a path fort. A minimal dominator that is also a path fort lacks any private omitted vertex; hence it has no adjacent selected vertices and must be the odd alternating word.
